title: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes
breakthrough: Consolidated guidelines for STEMI and Non-ST-elevation ACS into a unified pathway, recommending potent P2Y12 inhibitors (ticagrelor or prasugrel) over clopidogrel and formalizing early high-intensity statin plus ezetimibe co-initiation.
impact: Issued jointly by the ACC, AHA, and affiliated emergency and interventional societies, updating standard medical therapy, invasive catheterization timelines, and bleeding risk reduction strategies.
practical: Mandates immediate upstream double-drug lipid lowering and routine PPI co-prescription for patients at high GI bleeding risk on dual antiplatelet therapy.

breakthrough: Published in NEJM, this trial evaluated baxdrostat, a selective aldosterone synthase inhibitor, demonstrating significant blood pressure reductions in patients with treatment-resistant hypertension without causing clinically significant hyperkalemia or adrenal insufficiency.
impact: Directly influenced updated AHA/ACC hypertension guidelines, adding aldosterone synthase inhibition as a novel class recommendation for refractory hypertension.
practical: Provides a targeted hormonal mechanism to lower blood pressure for patients who fail triple-therapy antihypertensive regimens (including mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists).

title: Early Discontinuation of Aspirin after PCI in Low-Risk Acute Myocardial Infarction (TARGET-FIRST Trial)
breakthrough: Evaluated 1-month DAPT followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy versus standard 12-month DAPT in post-PCI acute MI patients, proving 1-month DAPT is non-inferior for ischemic protection while significantly reducing moderate-to-severe bleeding.
impact: Directly accelerated the shift in post-PCI guidelines toward dropping aspirin after 30 days in favor of single P2Y12 monotherapy for low-to-intermediate risk MI patients.
practical: Allows clinicians to routinely stop aspirin 4 weeks after stenting, cutting major bleeding complications by more than half without increasing stent thrombosis risk.

title: Tirzepatide in Patients with Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity (SUMMIT Trial)

impact: Re-defined valvular heart disease guidelines, shifting early TAVR from a class IIb to a class I recommendation when early cardiac structural strain or fibrosis is present.
practical: Changes clinical monitoring for asymptomatic aortic stenosis by adding non-invasive fibrosis screening to trigger intervention before symptoms develop.

title: Discontinuation vs. Continuation of Aspirin in Patients on Chronic Oral Anticoagulation (OAC-ALONE 2 Trial)
breakthrough: Showed that combining antiplatelet agents (like aspirin) with long-term oral anticoagulants in stable CAD patients markedly increases major bleeding and overall mortality without providing added protection against MI or stroke.
impact: Formalized international consensus recommendations to de-escalate dual antithrombotic therapy to oral anticoagulant (DOAC) monotherapy in patients with stable coronary disease beyond 1 year post-PCI or ACS.
practical: Instructs primary cardiologists to deprescribe routine daily aspirin in patients who are established on full-dose oral anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation or VTE.

title: Intracoronary Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) vs. Angiography Guidance for Complex PCI (OCCAMI Trial)
breakthrough: Published in The Lancet, this trial demonstrated that OCT-guided intravascular imaging leads to significantly lower rates of target vessel failure, stent thrombosis, and cardiac death compared to standard angiography-guided stenting in complex lesions.
impact: Upgraded intravascular imaging (OCT/IVUS) to a Class I guideline requirement during complex percutaneous coronary interventions (such as bifurcations, left main, or chronic total occlusions).
practical: Drives catheterization labs to adopt routine intravascular imaging rather than relying solely on luminogram angiograms to optimize stent expansion and strut apposition.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion vs. NOACs in High-Bleeding-Risk Atrial Fibrillation (CLOSURE-AF Trial)
breakthrough: Evaluated transcatheter left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) against novel oral anticoagulants in patients with non-valvular AF and high bleeding risk, proving non-inferiority for stroke prevention with a dramatic reduction in life-threatening bleeding.
impact: Updated stroke prevention guidelines to recommend LAAC as an early, first-line alternative to NOACs for patients with high HAS-BLED scores rather than reserving it purely as a rescue therapy.
practical: Expands interventional electrophysiology referral pathways for patients unable to tolerate long-term oral anticoagulation due to recurrent bleeding or severe anemia risk.

title: Intravenous Tenecteplase vs. Alteplase Prior to Endovascular Thrombectomy for Ischemic Stroke (TIMELESS-2 Trial)
breakthrough: Demonstrated in NEJM that IV tenecteplase (a single bolus tissue plasminogen activator) yields superior early reperfusion rates and better 90-day functional independence compared to alteplase infusion before mechanical thrombectomy.
impact: Jointly endorsed by AHA/ASA and neuro-cardiology consensus panels, establishing tenecteplase as the primary first-line thrombolytic agent for acute ischemic stroke with large-vessel occlusion.
practical: Simplifies acute emergency stroke protocols by replacing continuous infusion pumps with a single intravenous bolus, saving crucial minutes during emergency interventional transfers.
